subject: Residency controls & cross-region failover — follow-up and actions
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lena Schmidt <lena.schmidt@novahealth.com>, David Cole <david.cole@novahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Residency controls & cross-region failover — follow-up and actions

Hi Lena / David,

Thanks again for the call earlier — good conversation and appreciate the clarity on your compliance constraints. Wife note of what we covered and the small set of clarifying items we promised to follow up on: 

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary production must store identifiable customer data (PII) only in EU regions for EU customers.
- Non-PII derived telemetry may be allowed in US for analytics; logs must be redacted/hashed before leaving EU.
- You need answers on cross-region failover behavior, RPO/RTO expectations, and how backups are stored & encrypted.

Open questions (please confirm):
1) Failure mode: If EU region loses availability, are you comfortable with a controlled failover to an EU-adjacent region (e.g., eu-west-1 hot standby) or do you require a strict single-region lockdown with manual DR? Please state preferred sequence (automatic failover vs manual).
2) Backups: For daily snapshots that contain configuration + minimal operational metadata, do those need to be geo-anchored in EU only, or is a geo-redundant copy allowed if it’s encrypted with a customer-managed key (CMK)?
3) Logging: You mentioned audit logs must not contain raw PII. Can you confirm which fields you consider PII for our sanitization rules (e.g., name, email, phone, user_id)?
4) Retention windows: What retention windows do you require for request/response logs and for full KV snapshots?

What we’ll do next (from Redwood):
- Share a short one-page residency summary (attached) that maps our model pinning and failover options to the scenarios we discussed.
- Provide a sanitized sample log template and a suggested redaction rule-set for your security team.
- Internal ops will draft an ops-playbook snippet for a canary failover — Ben + Jonas will lead that and propose a test window.

Attachments: 2027-04-20_residency-summary.pdf (one-pager), ops-playbook-snapshot.txt (excerpt)

Proposed next steps:
- Lena: confirm items 1–4 above by end of week so we can size the EU-only configuration and quote any Dedicated/EU private options.
- Redwood: Ben to follow up with an EU canary calendar (30–60m window) and a draft price delta for dedicated EU capacity vs hosted.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short follow-up if that helps (15–20m).

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole

From: Lena Schmidt <lena.schmidt@novahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: David Cole <david.cole@novahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 10:42:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Residency controls & cross-region failover — follow-up and actions

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers inline below and a few clarifying asks.

1) Failure mode: We prefer automatic failover within EU regions (eu-west -> eu-central) for availability, but only for read-heavy operations. For write-heavy, we require controlled/manual failover with pre-approved checklist (to avoid accidental cross-border writes).

2) Backups: Geo-redundant copies are acceptable provided they are encrypted with our CMK and the secondary copy is still within EU boundaries. If the secondary would be outside EU, that is unacceptable.

3) Logging/PII: PII includes name, email, phone, national ID numbers, and any free-text that could contain identifiers. We need redaction rules for email and phone at a minimum; user_id pseudonyms are OK if they are irreversible hashes.

4) Retention: Audit logs — 3 years; request/response logs (full) — 90 days; sanitized analytics — 5 years.

We also flagged a couple items for our security team: proof of encryption-at-rest key lifecycle, access control audit for the private control plane, and list of CSP regions where backups would physically reside. Attaching our initial questionnaire (nova_compliance-q_v1.xlsx) — it's high level but should help map responsibilities.

Can Ben/Marissa propose a two-hour canary test plan for EU failover (including which endpoints we will hit and rollback criteria)? We prefer a weekday afternoon window next week if you have capacity.

Thanks,
Lena
Lena Schmidt
Head of Platform Security | Nova Health
Lena.Schmidt@novahealth.com

Attachment: nova_compliance-q_v1.xlsx

Folks — quick internal/proposal note before we lock dates: 

Proposed approach (high level)
- EU-only production: pin model serving and storage to EU regions. Use EU CMK (customer-managed) for snapshots and S3-equivalent backups. No outbound backups to US.
- Failover: configure *automatic* read-only failover across EU zones for availability; for writes, implement a manual canary + DR runbook where Redwood opens a controlled failover ticket (requires Nova sign-off).
- Logging: Redwood will ship only redacted logs by default. We will provide a redaction rule-set and an adjustable pipeline so Nova can request additional fields be hashed/removed.

Sizing & pricing note
- If Nova wants Dedicated EU GPUs for predictable latency and isolation, we'll include a 12-month reserved option. I estimate a modest price delta (~12–18%) versus hosted EU capacity — final after we confirm throughput numbers.

Canary test
- Proposed window: Tue 27 Apr 2027 14:00–16:00 CET (Marissa / Ben to own execution). Steps will include: baseline traffic validation, intentional zone failover (read path), verification of redaction rules, rollback, and post-mortem template. Jonas will draft the runbook.

Next internal actions
- Jonas: create the ops-playbook-snapshot.txt (first draft attached in earlier mail).
- Marissa: confirm the proposed canary window with Nova.
- Ben: prepare a preliminary Dedicated EU delta and send a short SKU list.

Ben
